Data Analysis: immune response

Immunity * sex interaction

Total_wbc: the total count of white blood cells circulating in the blood stream

# Prepare variables
data$treatment <- factor(data$treatment,
                       levels = c("control", "low", "high"))

data$sex <- factor(data$sex)
data$tank_id <- factor(data$tank_id)
data$body_mass_sc <- scale(data$body_mass)

# Total WBC interaction model
m1_wbc_int <- glmmTMB(
  total_wbc ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m1_wbc_int)
##  Family: Gamma  ( log )
## Formula:          total_wbc ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   1177.7   1205.1   -579.8   1159.7      147 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance  Std.Dev. 
##  tank_id (Intercept) 5.846e-10 2.418e-05
## Number of obs: 156, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for Gamma family (sigma^2): 0.0942 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                       Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)            3.48472    0.06201   56.20   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow          -0.02087    0.08599   -0.24   0.8083    
## treatmenthigh          0.09630    0.08770    1.10   0.2722    
## sexmale                0.08120    0.08678    0.94   0.3494    
## body_mass_sc          -0.04187    0.02511   -1.67   0.0954 .  
## treatmentlow:sexmale  -0.02144    0.12041   -0.18   0.8586    
## treatmenthigh:sexmale -0.20607    0.12068   -1.71   0.0877 .  
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
res_wbc_int <- simulateResiduals(m1_wbc_int)
plot(res_wbc_int)

testDispersion(res_wbc_int)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.0128, p-value = 0.936
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_wbc_int)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_wbc_int
## outliers at both margin(s) = 3, observations = 156, p-value = 0.1293
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.003983542 0.055169937
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                             0.01923077
Anova(m1_wbc_int, type = "III")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: total_wbc
##                   Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
## (Intercept)   3157.9818  1    < 2e-16 ***
## treatment        2.0408  2    0.36045    
## sex              0.8755  1    0.34943    
## body_mass_sc     2.7811  1    0.09538 .  
## treatment:sex    3.5227  2    0.17182    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
emmeans(
  m1_wbc_int,
  pairwise ~ treatment | sex,
  type = "response",
  adjust = "tukey"
)
## $emmeans
## sex = female:
##  treatment response   SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##  control       32.6 2.02 Inf      28.9      36.8
##  low           31.9 1.93 Inf      28.4      36.0
##  high          35.9 2.27 Inf      31.7      40.6
## 
## sex = male:
##  treatment response   SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##  control       35.4 2.11 Inf      31.5      39.8
##  low           33.9 2.07 Inf      30.1      38.2
##  high          31.7 1.84 Inf      28.3      35.5
## 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale 
## 
## $contrasts
## sex = female:
##  contrast       ratio     SE  df null z.ratio p.value
##  control / low  1.021 0.0878 Inf    1   0.243  0.9681
##  control / high 0.908 0.0796 Inf    1  -1.098  0.5152
##  low / high     0.889 0.0773 Inf    1  -1.349  0.3682
## 
## sex = male:
##  contrast       ratio     SE  df null z.ratio p.value
##  control / low  1.043 0.0880 Inf    1   0.502  0.8705
##  control / high 1.116 0.0925 Inf    1   1.325  0.3813
##  low / high     1.070 0.0896 Inf    1   0.805  0.6997
## 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates 
## Tests are performed on the log scale
emmeans(
  m1_wbc_int,
  pairwise ~ sex | treatment,
  type = "response",
  adjust = "tukey"
)
## $emmeans
## treatment = control:
##  sex    response   SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##  female     32.6 2.02 Inf      28.9      36.8
##  male       35.4 2.11 Inf      31.5      39.8

##  male       33.9 2.07 Inf      30.1      38.2

## treatment = high:

##  female     35.9 2.27 Inf      31.7      40.6
##  male       31.7 1.84 Inf      28.3      35.5

## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale

Plotting: WBC x sex

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Prepare labels
#---------------------------------------------------------

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control", "low", "high")),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    ),
    sex_plot = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("female", "male"),
      labels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  )

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Colour palettes for sex
# Same as previous sex-split behavioural plots
#---------------------------------------------------------

sex_pastel_cols <- c(
  "Female" = "#D8B4E2",
  "Male"   = "#A9CCE3"
)


sex_dark_cols <- c(
  "Female" = "#8E44AD",
  "Male"   = "#2874A6"
)

pd <- position_dodge(width = 0.75)

pj <- position_jitterdodge(
  jitter.width = 0.12,
  dodge.width = 0.75
)

#=========================================================
# 1) TOTAL WBC
#=========================================================

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Estimated marginal means
#---------------------------------------------------------

emm_wbc_int_df <- as.data.frame(
  emmeans(
    m1_wbc_int,
    ~ sex | treatment,
    type = "response"
  )
)

cn <- names(emm_wbc_int_df)

mean_col <- dplyr::first(cn[cn %in% c("response", "rate", "emmean")])

lower_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^lower\\.CL$|^asymp\\.LCL$|^LCL$|^lower$", cn)]
)

upper_col <- dplyr::first(
  cn[grepl("^upper\\.CL$|^asymp\\.UCL$|^UCL$|^upper$", cn)]
)

emm_wbc_int_df <- emm_wbc_int_df %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("control", "low", "high")),
    sex = factor(sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    ),
    sex_plot = factor(
      sex,
      levels = c("female", "male"),
      labels = c("Female", "Male")
    )
  ) %>%
  rename(
    mean  = !!mean_col,
    lower = !!lower_col,
    upper = !!upper_col
  )

#---------------------------------------------------------
# Plot total WBC
#---------------------------------------------------------

p_wbc_sex <- ggplot() +

  geom_violin(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = total_wbc,
      fill = sex_plot,
      group = interaction(treatment_plot, sex_plot)
    ),
    position = pd,
    trim = FALSE,
    alpha = 0.25,
    colour = NA,
    linewidth = 0
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = data,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = total_wbc,
      colour = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pj,
    alpha = 0.55,
    size = 2
  ) +

  geom_errorbar(
    data = emm_wbc_int_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      ymin = lower,
      ymax = upper,
      colour = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pd,
    width = 0.18,
    linewidth = 1.3
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = emm_wbc_int_df,
    aes(
      x = treatment_plot,
      y = mean,
      fill = sex_plot,
      group = sex_plot
    ),
    position = pd,
    shape = 21,
    size = 5,
    stroke = 1.2,
    colour = "black"
  ) +

  scale_colour_manual(values = sex_dark_cols) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = sex_pastel_cols) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(8),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))
  ) +

  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Total white blood cells",
    fill = "Sex",
    colour = "Sex"
  ) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +

  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 13),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 15),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 13)
  )

print(p_wbc_sex)

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "total_wbc_treatment_sex_side_by_side.pdf"),
  plot = p_wbc_sex,
  width = 7,
  height = 5
)

ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "total_wbc_treatment_sex_side_by_side.jpg"),
  plot = p_wbc_sex,
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 600
)

Main effects model

m1_wbc <- glmmTMB(
  total_wbc ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m1_wbc)
##  Family: Gamma  ( log )
## Formula:          total_wbc ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   1177.2   1198.5   -581.6   1163.2      149 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance  Std.Dev. 
##  tank_id (Intercept) 1.759e-09 4.194e-05
## Number of obs: 156, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for Gamma family (sigma^2): 0.0962 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)    3.525430   0.051298   68.72   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow  -0.033561   0.060889   -0.55    0.582    
## treatmenthigh -0.011693   0.060875   -0.19    0.848    
## sexmale        0.004208   0.051949    0.08    0.935    
## body_mass_sc  -0.039908   0.025303   -1.58    0.115    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
simulationOutput <- simulateResiduals(m1_wbc)
plot(simulationOutput)

testDispersion(simulationOutput)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.0197, p-value = 0.872
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(simulationOutput)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## outliers at both margin(s) = 1, observations = 156, p-value = 1
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.0001622805 0.0351967007
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                            0.006410256
Anova(m1_wbc, type = "II")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type II Wald chisquare tests)

Immunity * sex interaction

N.L_ratio: neutrophil-to-lymphocye ratio. Two of the most abundant white blood cells.

# N:L ratio interaction model
m1_nl_int <- glmmTMB(
  n.l_ratio ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m1_nl_int)
##  Family: Gamma  ( log )
## Formula:          n.l_ratio ~ treatment * sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   -271.4   -244.0    144.7   -289.4      147 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  tank_id (Intercept) 0.03082  0.1756  
## Number of obs: 156, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for Gamma family (sigma^2): 0.263 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                        Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)           -1.516465   0.120927 -12.540   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow          -0.171875   0.171614  -1.002    0.317    
## treatmenthigh         -0.101078   0.173740  -0.582    0.561    
## sexmale                0.038974   0.145499   0.268    0.789    
## body_mass_sc          -0.007033   0.045443  -0.155    0.877    
## treatmentlow:sexmale   0.063979   0.209383   0.306    0.760    
## treatmenthigh:sexmale -0.299387   0.209072  -1.432    0.152    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
res_nl_int <- simulateResiduals(m1_nl_int)
plot(res_nl_int)

testDispersion(res_nl_int)

## 
##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.
##  simulated
## 
## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.1025, p-value = 0.6
## alternative hypothesis: two.sided
testOutliers(res_nl_int)

## 
##  DHARMa outlier test based on exact binomial test with approximate
##  expectations
## 
## data:  res_nl_int
## outliers at both margin(s) = 2, observations = 156, p-value = 0.3532
## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.001556412 0.045543016
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                             0.01282051
Anova(m1_nl_int, type = "III")
## Analysis of Deviance Table (Type III Wald chisquare tests)
## 
## Response: n.l_ratio
##                  Chisq Df Pr(>Chisq)    
## (Intercept)   157.2601  1     <2e-16 ***
## treatment       1.0147  2     0.6021    
## sex             0.0718  1     0.7888    
## body_mass_sc    0.0240  1     0.8770    
## treatment:sex   3.3077  2     0.1913    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
emmeans(
  m1_nl_int,
  pairwise ~ treatment | sex,
  type = "response",
  adjust = "tukey"
)
## $emmeans
## sex = female:
##  treatment response     SE  df asymp.LCL asymp.UCL
##  control      0.219 0.0265 Inf     0.173     0.278
##  low          0.185 0.0226 Inf     0.145     0.235
##  high         0.198 0.0250 Inf     0.155     0.254
## 
## sex = male:

##  high         0.153 0.0181 Inf     0.121     0.193
## 
## Confidence level used: 0.95 
## Intervals are back-transformed from the log scale 
## 
## $contrasts
## sex = female:
##  contrast       ratio    SE  df null z.ratio p.value
##  control / low  1.188 0.204 Inf    1   1.002  0.5759
##  control / high 1.106 0.192 Inf    1   0.582  0.8299
##  low / high     0.932 0.163 Inf    1  -0.405  0.9137
## 
## sex = male:

##  control / high 1.493 0.248 Inf    1   2.406  0.0427
##  low / high     1.340 0.227 Inf    1   1.725  0.1958
## 
## P value adjustment: tukey method for comparing a family of 3 estimates

emmeans(
  m1_nl_int,

Main effects model

# 1) Prepare variables
data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high")
    ),
    sex = factor(sex),
    tank_id = factor(tank_id),
    body_mass_sc = as.numeric(scale(body_mass)),
    treatment_plot = factor(
      treatment,
      levels = c("control", "low", "high"),
      labels = c("Control", "Low", "High")
    )
  )


# 2) Model: Gamma GLMM

m1_nl <- glmmTMB(
  n.l_ratio ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id),
  family = Gamma(link = "log"),
  data = data
)

summary(m1_nl)
##  Family: Gamma  ( log )
## Formula:          n.l_ratio ~ treatment + sex + body_mass_sc + (1 | tank_id)
## Data: data
## 
##      AIC      BIC   logLik deviance df.resid 
##   -272.1   -250.8    143.1   -286.1      149 
## 
## Random effects:
## 
## Conditional model:
##  Groups  Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  tank_id (Intercept) 0.03011  0.1735  
## Number of obs: 156, groups:  tank_id, 24
## 
## Dispersion estimate for Gamma family (sigma^2): 0.268 
## 
## Conditional model:
##                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)   -1.475682   0.106505 -13.855   <2e-16 ***
## treatmentlow  -0.139148   0.134805  -1.032   0.3020    
## treatmenthigh -0.255984   0.134367  -1.905   0.0568 .  
## sexmale       -0.038045   0.090330  -0.421   0.6736    
## body_mass_sc  -0.005248   0.045672  -0.115   0.9085    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# 3) Diagnostics

res_nl <- simulateResiduals(m1_nl)
plot(res_nl)

testDispersion(res_nl)

##  DHARMa nonparametric dispersion test via sd of residuals fitted vs.

## data:  simulationOutput
## dispersion = 1.1016, p-value = 0.528

testOutliers(res_nl)

## alternative hypothesis: true probability of success is not equal to 0.007968127
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  0.001556412 0.045543016
## sample estimates:
## frequency of outliers (expected: 0.00796812749003984 ) 
##                                             0.01282051
# 4) Type II ANOVA
Anova(m1_nl, type = "II")

## body_mass_sc 0.0132  1     0.9085
anova(m1_nl, m1_nl_int)

  dpi = 600
)
# IMMUNE-RESPONSE PANEL WITHOUT SEX SEPARATION

# Remove the previous hard upper limit of 80 from the WBC plot.
# This ensures that all raw WBC observations are retained.
p_wbc_main_panel <- p_wbc +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 7),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, NA)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Total white blood cells"
  )
## Scale for y is already present.
## Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale.
# Prepare the N:L-ratio plot with matching formatting
p_nl_main_panel <- p_nl +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 7),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, NA)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio"
  )
## Scale for y is already present.
## Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale.
# Combine the two immune-response figures
immune_panel_main <- (
  p_wbc_main_panel |
  p_nl_main_panel
) +
  plot_annotation(
    tag_levels = "A"
  ) &
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",

    plot.tag = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),

    plot.tag.position = c(0, 1),

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 15
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 13,
      colour = "grey25"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 10,
      b = 10,
      l = 10
    )
  )

# Display the complete panel
immune_panel_main

# Save as PDF for the manuscript
ggsave(
  filename = here::here(
    "figures",
    "immune_responses_main_panel.pdf"
  ),
  plot = immune_panel_main,
  width = 12,
  height = 5.5,
  units = "in",
  device = cairo_pdf
)

# Save a high-resolution JPG version
ggsave(
  filename = here::here(
    "figures",
    "immune_responses_main_panel.jpg"
  ),
  plot = immune_panel_main,
  width = 12,
  height = 5.5,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600,
  bg = "white"
)
# IMMUNE-RESPONSE PANEL SEPARATED BY SEX

# Prepare the WBC plot
p_wbc_supp_panel_tagged <- p_wbc_sex +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 7),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, NA)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Total white blood cells",
    colour = "Sex",
    fill = "Sex"
  )
## Scale for y is already present.
## Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale.
# Prepare the N:L-ratio plot
p_nl_supp_panel_tagged <- p_nl_sex +
  scale_y_continuous(
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 7),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.08))
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    ylim = c(0, NA)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Fluoxetine treatment",
    y = "Neutrophil:lymphocyte ratio",
    colour = "Sex",
    fill = "Sex"
  )
## Scale for y is already present.
## Adding another scale for y, which will replace the existing scale.
# Combine plots and collect the identical sex legends
immune_panel_sex <- (
  p_wbc_supp_panel_tagged |
  p_nl_supp_panel_tagged
) +
  patchwork::plot_layout(
    guides = "collect"
  ) &
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),

    # Place the shared legend at the upper-right
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "right",
    legend.box.just = "right",

    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 13
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 12
    ),

    legend.margin = margin(
      t = 0,
      r = 10,
      b = 4,
      l = 0
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 15
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 13,
      colour = "grey25"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 12,
      r = 10,
      b = 10,
      l = 10
    )
  )


# Display the complete supplementary panel
immune_panel_sex

# Save as PDF
ggsave(
